decision.reason: The frozen WaveC route and accepted C1 run prove QNN/HTP ReLU tensor consumption by the OpenCL bridge. They do not provide a full-Gemma QNN/HTP forward tensor or a real language-model loss/update consuming that tensor.

engineering_translation: Keep the hybrid route: QNN/HTP for static forward islands after compile/runtime proof; Adreno/OpenCL remains mainline for mutable adapter update.
Treat the observed tiny-ReLU 548.272958 ms as host-observed qnn-net-run wall time, not isolated HTP device compute.
Add QNN profile parsing before scaling: separate qnn-net-run wall, context load, RPC or accelerator execute, and file transfer when available.
Prefer qnn-profile-viewer/profiling logs plus repeat-inference or throughput mode when practical.

Replace gemma_hidden2560_relu with the smallest Gemma decoder/forward island preserving [1,16,2560] float32_le output, then prove that tensor is consumed by the existing OpenCL adapter/loss/update bridge.
route_falsifiers: If QNN profile parsing shows the tiny ReLU graph itself really takes near 548 ms accelerator time, the host-wall interpretation is wrong and the runtime envelope needs redesign.

If the smallest Gemma island fails QNN compile/runtime, emits unsupported-op fields, changes shape/dtype, cannot be consumed by OpenCL, or leaves adapter pre/post unchanged, fail closed with the exact field.

why_existing_sources_are_not_enough.limitation: Runs QNN graph gemma_hidden2560_relu and records expected ReLU parity; it does not run a Gemma decoder block or language-model objective.
Consumes a [1,16,2560] float32 tensor in an OpenCL rank-16 MSE adapter cell and reports cross-entropy unavailable for the bounded bridge.
Sets forward_cross_entropy, perplexity, answer_token_accuracy, calibration, and probability-distribution metrics to unavailable for the bounded polar MSE bridge.
Builds Gemma-compatible identity/ReLU HTP context artifacts, not a full-Gemma decoder or LM-head-facing QNN graph.

smallest_falsifiable_next_implementation.owner: Phase3/4 engineering with active Research signal lane
smallest_falsifiable_next_implementation.action: Create a bounded full-Gemma QNN/HTP forward producer for one fixed-shape [1,16,2560] float32_le hidden-tensor route, then feed its output into the existing OpenCL adapter-update consumer or a real teacher-forced LM-loss consumer.
minimum_source_delta: Add a host/phone runner that accepts a full-Gemma QNN context path, graph name, fixed input tensor identity, expected output bytes, and report path.
Add validation that rejects graph names gemma_hidden2560_relu and gemma_hidden2560_identity_add for this gate.

Add report fields for QNN/HTP context path/SHA, graph name, backend, tensor shape/dtype/bytes/SHA, raw boundary, profiling, consumer input SHA, loss/update identity, and CPU/OpenCL/QNN fallback flags.
Add QNN profile parsing for qnn-profile-viewer/profiling logs and separate host-observed qnn-net-run wall time from context load, RPC or accelerator execute, and file transfer fields where available.
Add a test that a report with only the ReLU graph or null cross-entropy cannot satisfy the full-Gemma consumed-tensor gate.
stop_if: No full-Gemma QNN context or graph identity is available.
QNN runtime falls back to CPU without explicit fallback status.
Phase4 consumes metadata instead of the raw tensor path.
The update is bridge MSE relabeled as LM loss.
Raw .pjp1, .raw, .f32.bin, model, checkpoint, adapter, or tensor payloads enter git.
